pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:200 A Weir pile whose packet id or run id will not parse is silently dropped from the rail, so an unreadable pending item is invisible on the decision surface instead of surfacing at the most severe bucket with a marker saying why.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:200 An unparseable pile is skipped with no marker and no log line. That is quieter than the mildest bucket, which is the failure this technique names.

app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:205 The rail is drawn from the system of record (good), and write errors are toasted (Board.tsx:103). Queue hygiene is missing: open packets never expire, nothing records 'expired unanswered', and the rail is not sorted by expiry or consequence.

app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:203 A pending summary carries openedAt but no severity and no deadline. No ladder exists, so no item is ever marked overdue. Same root cause as the review-queues hygiene gap.

app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:245 The commit is one kernel transaction that carries the preview token, a fresh v1 digest and an idempotency ticket. The kernel refuses a stale preview, so approval binds to a version.
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:74 Every patch, pick, undo, commit and return is written with who, the surface and the operator role.
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:222 The preview's consequence is derived by the source adapter from the bound v1 state and the recorded decisions, not from a self-description.

app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:249 The commit enqueues and kicks the apply outbox. DecidedDesk shows the apply state (pending, applied or stuck) with v1's error verbatim, and a stuck apply can be redriven (actions.ts:82).

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:193 When a live launch comes back stale after the operator's K, the apply swaps in the fresh receipt and launches it without asking again (bounded only by a ceiling re-priced at apply time), so what runs can differ from what the operator was shown.

techniques.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:193 The technique says a stale-world resume asks again or fails loudly. Here the fresh receipt is launched once. The /produce Receipt (Receipt.tsx:9-11) does the opposite and shows the changes before a re-confirm. Mitigations: an interrupted confirm is failed, never re-launched (spend.ts:213), and a project subject pins its revision (spendLive.ts:76).
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:164 An agent's keep cannot open the spend gate. Only an operator decision previews into a live launch.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:204 The applier enforces the truncation as well as the preview, so an agent has no expression for 'spend' at either component.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:167 The disclosure is in units of consequence (what, provider/model lines, total), read from the live receipt.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:226 A refusal carries its reasons and note back to the requesting agent. A reasonless reject is skipped and named.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:262 Spend piles are derived from every request still 'requested' in the kernel store, so the queue is complete by construction.

pairs.registryProposal: resume-after-decision could settle whether a fresh receipt launched under a dollar ceiling taken from the confirmed card counts as 'what was shown'. This code treats the ceiling as the consent boundary; the technique, read literally, requires a re-ask.
